1.explanation:
• DrilldownBreadcrumbs.js: this component builds and handles clicks on the breadcrumb trail; it’s where setRootElement is called with the wrong target when the subprocess is wrapped by a pool.  
• DrilldownUtil.js: contains helper logic for finding and normalizing drill-down roots; it doesn’t account for the extra pool wrapper and therefore returns undefined.  
• SubprocessCompatibility.js: adapts drill-down behavior for collapsed subprocesses; needs to include logic for pool-wrapped subprocesses.  
• DrilldownOverlayBehavior.js: listens for root changes to update overlays; because the root change never properly fires, overlays aren’t reattached on drill out.  
• UpdateCanvasRootHandler.js: the command handler for changing the canvas root; it must correctly wire up the new rootElement for undo/redo and event firing.  
• Canvas.js: implements setRootElement and throws the error when no valid rootElement is passed; it surfaces the bug and its guardrail may need to be adjusted once the callers are fixed.
1.bug_scenario: When drilling into a collapsed subprocess that’s wrapped by a pool, clicking the breadcrumb to drill back out triggers a call to Canvas.setRootElement with an undefined rootElement. This throws “rootElement required” and leaves you stuck inside the subprocess.

2.explanation:
• DrilldownBreadcrumbs.js – contains the click handler that invokes canvas.setRootElement; because the overlay hasn’t updated its stored root, it ends up passing undefined and throws the error.  
• DrilldownOverlayBehavior.js – registers the drilldown overlay on the diagram, but never listens for or reacts to canvas root change events (e.g. when a collapsed subprocess under a pool becomes the new root).  
• DrilldownCentering.js – meant to re-center the viewport on the active root, but isn’t triggered on drill-out in the pool/subprocess scenario, so the overlay remains out of sync.  
• SubprocessCompatibility.js – adds compatibility fixes for collapsed subprocesses, but doesn’t handle the additional pool wrapper, so the drilldown utilities never resolve the true parent root.  
• DrilldownUtil.js – helper functions that compute drilldown targets; they don’t accommodate the extra pool level, leading to missing/undefined root references when building breadcrumbs.  
• UpdateCanvasRootHandler.js – the modeling command that actually performs canvas.setRootElement; although it correctly sets the new root when drilling in, it isn’t wired into the drilldown overlay lifecycle, so drilling back out never invokes it with a valid element.
2.bug_scenario: When I wrap a collapsed subprocess inside a pool, navigate into that subprocess, and then click the breadcrumb back to the parent process, the library throws “Uncaught Error: rootElement required.” In the drill-out click handler (in DrilldownBreadcrumbs.js), canvas.setRootElement is called with an undefined element. In other words, after I drill into the subprocess the drilldown overlay never picks up the new root, so when I try to drill back out it has no valid rootElement to pass to the canvas.
